historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease principal): FY2021 27.9, FY2023 23.8, FY2026 60.1. CAGRs run to FY2026 from FY2023 (3yr) and FY2021 (5yr). The owner-FCF CAGRs exceed the reported-FCF CAGRs not because SBC is shrinking (it is nil) but because the lease-principal deduction is a near-fixed subtraction that makes the smaller owner series more geared to the FY2026 step-up, and because FY2026 carries a ~NZ$15m working-capital inflow; neither CAGR is a usable forward growth anchor.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Unchanged from the prior build: blend of the equity 5yr CAGR (9.7%) and the revenue 5yr CAGR (9.9%), haircut for the maturity of the NZ segments and management's own caution that early-FY2027 trading is not indicative. Equity CAGR is still understated as a growth signal because HLG pays out ~70-90% of earnings as dividends (FY2026 DPS 69c on EPS 99c).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (13.7%) diverges >30% from EPS 3yr CAGR (22.4%). Not a quality flag: FY2023 was the post-COVID cost-inflation trough (NPAT NZ$32.0m) and FY2026 the record (NZ$59.2m), so the 3yr EPS CAGR is a trough-to-peak recovery; retained earnings lag because most profit leaves as dividends. 5yr CAGRs (equity 9.7%, revenue 9.9%, EPS 12.1%) are within band.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue, EPS and equity CAGRs from the Metrics CSV annual rows FY2021/FY2023/FY2026. EPS is in NZ dollars (FY2026 basic 0.992).

scenario_narratives.base: Glassons Australia keeps compounding from a NZ$324m base at a decelerating rate as the store count (41 at year end) grows by a few units a year and the new automated Sydney warehouse lifts online and store replenishment; Glassons NZ and Hallensteins grow with the NZ consumer at low-to-mid single digits with Hallensteins' margin repair (pre-tax profit +129% in FY2026) holding. Group revenue grows 10% in FY2027 and fades to 4% by FY2036. Gross margin gives back part of FY2026's 240bps gain as the AUD and freight tailwinds normalise, so cash-EBIT settles at ~13.8-14.0% rather than the 14.25% just printed. Working capital absorbs 6% of each year's revenue increase, capex normalises to ~3.3% after the DC programme, and cash tax eases from 30.5% to 29% on the NZ/AU mix. Gordon binds the terminal value (implied exit below the 14x cap).
scenario_narratives.bull: The +18.4% constant-currency start holds through Black Friday and Christmas, so FY2027 grows 15%, and Australia then keeps double-digit growth for three more years as Glassons takes share from department stores and Cotton On while the Sydney DC removes the distribution constraint; Hallensteins' Australian rollout (6 stores) becomes a second growth leg. The full-price sell-through and sourcing discipline behind the 61.7% gross margin prove structural, lifting EBITDA to 24.6% and cash-EBIT to 15.5% as the lease base leverages (6.4 -> 6.2% of revenue). Terminal growth 2.5%, cap 15x.
scenario_narratives.bear: A soft NZ and Australian consumer plus Shein/Temu/Kmart price pressure cap FY2027 at 5% and growth at 2-3% thereafter; the AUD translation tailwind reverses and a stronger USD against unhedged purchases compresses gross margin, while the enlarged lease base (NZ$110.6m, Sydney DC and new stores) deleverages against flat sales. Cash-EBIT falls from 14.25% to ~10.3%, back toward the FY2022-23 trough, working capital absorbs 9% of revenue growth as markdowns rise, and the terminal cap is 12x on a structurally slower business. The balance sheet (no debt, NZ$88m cash) means the bear case is an earnings and multiple story, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the owner's cash: post-IFRS-16 EBITDA less the full cash lease charge, ex-ROU depreciation, cash tax, maintenance-plus-growth capex and the working capital that an inventory-heavy retailer consumes as it grows, with NZ$88.2m of net cash added once (interest income stripped from the flows) and lease liabilities kept out of net debt because their service cost is already in the flows. Ten-year explicit horizon because Australian growth is still decelerating; terminal value is the lower of Gordon at 2.25% and 14x terminal FCF. No SBC band, no NCI, no FX bridge: NZD flows, NZD quote.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gross margin: the FY2026 61.7% embeds AUD strength and lower freight; a 100bps give-back is roughly NZ$0.5/share of value
Australian growth durability from a NZ$324m base; the base case's 10% -> 4% fade is a judgment, not guidance, and the December AGM trading update is the next evidence
Lease base stepped up to NZ$110.6m; under treatment B this is in the flows at 6.4% of revenue, so a sales miss deleverages faster than the pre-DC fleet did

Working-capital capture of -6%/-9% vs the FY2026 +NZ$15m inflow: if the inflow is structural (supplier terms, DC) the model is ~NZ$0.3/share too low; if it reverses in FY2027 owner FCF prints below the model's Y1
Seasonality: Black Friday and Christmas dominate; the +18.4% start covers under a sixth of the year

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 9.20-15.29
data_sources.financials: HLG.NZ_Metrics.csv (H1-2017 to FY2026) and the FY2026 Annual Report (year ended 1 August 2026): cash flow statement for lease principal, lease interest, tax paid, capex and interest income; note 4.1 lease liabilities; note 2.4 diluted EPS for the share count; depreciation note for right-of-use depreciation 28.966
data_sources.qualitative: HLG.NZ_Analysis.json refreshed 2026-11-02: FY2026 results of 29 September 2026, segment mix, Sydney warehouse, eight-week FY2027 trading update and management caution

prior_version.note: Hand-built DCF on an FY2025 base (file last price-refreshed 2026-10-18); accounting-EBIT margin with separate lease principal/interest lines and per-scenario WACC 10.0/10.5/11.5.

bridge.item: Anchor refresh: net cash 58.3 -> 88.2 (FY2026 balance sheet) and diluted shares 59.649 -> 59.677

Base-year roll-forward to FY2026 actual: revenue 563.0 vs 522.5 the prior base modelled, cash-EBIT 14.25% vs ~12.2% modelled, horizon rolled one year, prior Y2-Y10 paths carried verbatim and translated to EBITDA/lease/D&A-ex-ROU components (translation is value-neutral by construction)

FY2027 guidance-year re-judgement (base growth 9 -> 10%, bull 12.5 -> 15%, bear 4 -> 5%; FY2027 capex 4.0%) and margin re-anchor to the FY2026 actual (prior ramp to the terminal margin replaced by a hold at it)
Methodology: single 10.5% WACC across scenarios (bull 10.0 -> 10.5 = -1.34 on bull, bear 11.5 -> 10.5 = +0.90 on bear), weighted

bridge.note: ties to probability_weighted.weighted_iv; measured by staged builds (roll-forward only 14.19; + re-judgement 15.16; + single WACC 15.05)

reconciliation.unchanged_judgments: Y2-Y10 growth paths in all three scenarios, working-capital capture (-6%/-9%), cash-tax paths (shifted one year), terminal growth (2.25/2.5/2.0), terminal caps (14/15/12), base WACC 10.5%, weights 25/50/25 and the 15% hurdle are the prior build's judgments carried forward. Evidence that would move them: an explicit Australian store-count plan or FY2027 guidance at the December AGM (growth path), a second year of 61%+ gross margin with a flat AUD (margin hold vs give-back), a reversal of the FY2026 working-capital inflow (capture rate), or a change in the NZ 10-year yield of more than ~50bps (WACC).

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 59.649m ordinary shares on issue (net of treasury stock) plus 0.028m LTIP performance rights per the FY2026 diluted-EPS note. Held FLAT: the only equity issuance is the LTIP, which is expensed as SBC (immaterial), and the company has not bought back shares since FY2021.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents NZ$78.205m plus NZ$10.0m short-term deposits (3-12 month term) at 1 August 2026; the Group has no interest-bearing borrowings (FY2026 AR note on interest-rate risk). Lease liabilities of NZ$110.6m (NZ$29.3m current + NZ$81.4m non-current, up from NZ$76.6m on the Sydney warehouse and new stores) are EXCLUDED from net debt under lease treatment B.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF = reported FCF 92.9 - SBC 0.1 - interest income 2.063 - lease principal repayments 30.619 (treatment B, same convention as the prior build's 40.66 for FY2025). FY2026 owner FCF is flattered by a ~NZ$15m working-capital inflow (payables timing around the Sydney DC commissioning) and depressed by Sydney-warehouse capex; the forward build normalises both.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report: NZ$0.099m share-based payment expense (LTIP performance rights); equity-award taxes nil across the whole history. Immaterial (0.02% of revenue), so the forward SBC path is held at 0.0% and the house/street band collapses.
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built, single rate across scenarios. NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5%, equity risk premium 5.5%, beta ~1.1 for a small/mid-cap NZX discretionary retailer gives a cost of equity of ~10.5%; with no interest-bearing debt WACC equals the cost of equity. Unchanged from the prior base-case 10.5%. The prior build also used 10.0% bull / 11.5% bear; that per-scenario spread is removed this update because scenario probability weighting already prices the cyclical and competitive risk in the flows (owner-fcf-adaptations section f, charge risk once). The effect on weighted IV is -NZ$0.11/share and is itemised in the reconciliation bridge.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. The full cash lease charge (principal 30.619 in financing + interest 5.530 in operating = 36.149, 6.42% of FY2026 revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (NZ$110.6m) are excluded from net debt; D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation (44.570 - 28.966 = 15.604, 2.77% of revenue). This is the same economic treatment as the prior build (which deducted lease principal and lease interest as separate lines against an accounting-EBIT margin); only the representation changed to fit the engine's components.
inputs.nci_treatment: none - no minority interests; all subsidiaries wholly owned
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row: operating company, non-US consumer retailer -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md for leases, NZD WACC and SBC-zero). Same model as the prior 2026-08-01 valuation; this is an UPDATE for the FY2026 result (year ended 1 August 2026), not a rebuild, with the prior driver paths carried forward one year and only the FY2027 guidance year and the margin anchor re-judged (see reconciliation). Anchors refreshed: price, net cash and diluted shares to the FY2026 balance sheet. FY2026 actuals in engine terms: post-IFRS-16 EBITDA 132.0 (23.4% of revenue), lease cash 6.42%, D&A ex-ROU 2.77%, cash-EBIT 14.25% (NZ$80.2m) versus accounting EBIT before lease interest of NZ$87.4m; cash tax paid 21.954 (27.4% of cash-EBIT; tax expense 24.756 was 29.5% of NPBT). FY2026 gross margin +240bps to 61.7% and constant-currency sales +15.6% (+19.6% reported, AUD translation tailwind). SBC-zero: house and street values coincide; band_position is null by construction, not a 0% reading. Buybacks: none since FY2021; the flat count is a modelling convention the company has not had to pay for, which is fine because SBC is immaterial. Working capital: inventory-heavy retailer, receivables negligible, so growth consumes cash; the -6% capture of the revenue increase (bear -9%) is kept from the prior build despite the FY2026 inflow, which is treated as timing. Price is the last regular NZX close, not an after-hours print.
inputs.model_rationale: A vertically-managed apparel retailer with no debt, immaterial SBC and a clear cash-flow stream is the textbook owner-FCF case; the only adaptations needed are IFRS 16 leases (treatment B), an NZD discount rate and the SBC-zero band collapse.

bear.rationale: Y1 re-judged 4.0% -> 5.0% (the strong start banks some H1 growth before a weak Christmas); Y2-Y10 are the prior bear path shifted. Cash-EBIT 12.7% in FY2027 fading to 10.3% terminal, matching the prior bear terminal (~10.6%): gross margin gives back the FX/freight gain and the enlarged lease base (6.6 -> 6.8%) deleverages against flat sales. WACC moved 11.5 -> 10.5 (single rate); bear risk is carried in the flows and the 25% weight.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 (Y1) re-judged 9.0% -> 10.0%: first eight weeks +18.4% cc, two NSW Glassons stores and one QLD Hallensteins store opened or due by October, Sydney DC live; held well below the run-rate because management says it will not persist and H2 FY2026 (+24.6%) is a brutal comp. Y2-Y10 are the prior build's path shifted one year (7.5 -> 4.0), unchanged: evidence that would move them is a FY2027 outcome above ~12% with constant-currency momentum into H2, or an explicit AU store-count target.
base.margin_rationale: Re-anchored to the FY2026 actual. Cash-EBIT (EBITDA 23.2 - lease 6.4 - D&A 2.8) is 14.0% in FY2027, a modest give-back from the 14.25% FY2026 actual (some of the 240bps gross-margin gain was AUD/freight tailwind), easing to 13.8% as the Sydney DC depreciates. The prior build's terminal margin translates to ~13.5-13.8% cash-EBIT, so the terminal level is effectively unchanged; what changed is that FY2026 already delivered it, so the prior ramp is replaced by a hold. Lease cost held at 6.4% (FY2026 actual 6.42%): new-store and DC leases offset leverage on the existing fleet.
base.capex_rationale: FY2027 4.0% (store openings, refurbishments and Sydney DC fit-out tail after FY2026's 5.2%), then the prior path 3.6 -> 3.3%. Tax path is the prior path shifted one year; 30.5% on cash-EBIT reproduces the FY2026 tax expense, easing to 29% as the NZ 28% / AU 30% mix settles.

bull.rationale: Y1 re-judged 12.5% -> 15.0% (the +18.4% cc start holds through Christmas); Y2-Y10 are the prior bull path shifted. Cash-EBIT 14.4% -> 15.5% terminal, matching the prior bull terminal (~15.4%) with lease leverage (6.4 -> 6.2%) as AU scales. WACC moved 10.0 -> 10.5 (single rate).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Unchanged from the prior build. Base 50%: a record FY2026 and strong FY2027 start tempered by management's own warning that eight weeks pre-Christmas are not indicative. Bull 25%: it needs the FX/freight-aided gross margin to prove structural AND Australian double-digit growth to persist from a much larger base, two independent things. Bear 25%, above the 15% house default, because the Analysis JSON's two high-severity risks (discretionary-spend sensitivity and online fast-fashion competition) are both live, earnings are now ~52% dependent on one segment (Glassons Australia), and USD purchases are unhedged; it is held below 30-35% because there is no going-concern, covenant or single-customer risk.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
